open.detail: UPDATE 2026-09-07 (offline repo read on main at 62638c17; no provider access). TWO of the four recorded claims hold, ONE holds with a corrected mechanism, and the central technical premise is REFUTED by the code on main. REFUTED: 'deletes an artifact family BEFORE calling OpenAI and re-inserting, one family at a time, never staged-then-swapped'. In all four writers in supabase/functions/indexing-v3-agent/index.ts - upsertMemoryCardsFromSections, upsertSectionIndexUnits, upsertVisualArtifacts, upsertCoreEmbeddingFields - the embeddingBatch await completes BEFORE sql.begin is entered, and the delete and re-insert share one Postgres transaction. A provider outage therefore aborts before any delete happens, and a failed insert rolls the delete back; the 'permanently empty family' failure mode does not follow from this code. tests/indexing-v3-agent.test.ts pins that ordering statically for all four. CONFIRMED: repair_strict_enrichment_gate_batch is invoked by nothing - every repo-wide hit is the migration, schema mirror, generated types, docs, or a schema-text assertion. CONFIRMED: no monitoring - needs_enrichment_artifacts appears in no script and no workflow. CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTED MECHANISM: both terminal states are excluded from claim eligibility forever, but by two different routes - claim_indexing_v3_agent_jobs excludes needs_enrichment_artifacts by NAME in 'status not in (...)', while failed is excluded through 'attempt_count < max_attempts', because agentFailureDecision only writes failed once attempts are spent. open.summary: Schema drift is gated against schema.sql only; the migration chain's semantics are never diffed against the mirror
open.detail: generate-drift-manifest.ts replays supabase/schema.sql and embeds ITS sha256; CI's db-reset-verify runs supabase migration up --local, proving the chain APPLIES but never diffing the result against schema.sql. A migration whose function or policy body diverges from the mirror passes every gate. Object-NAME parity does hold today (all create targets across 211 migrations resolve into schema.sql) but it is enforced by hand-written per-object tests, not systematically. FIX: after migration up --local, replay schema.sql into a second scratch database and diff schema_drift_snapshot() between the two. Fully offline and containerised, no provider access. Run 34104496596 (c8cc72f), job 101689976803, started 09:22:47Z and completed 10:33:07Z = 70m20s, identical shape. Both land exactly on the configured timeout. GitHub reports a timed-out job as cancelled, and one cancelled job makes the whole run conclusion cancelled. That is the entire explanation for main's run-level redness, and it also explains the earlier temporal pattern (runs stopped concluding cancelled when the merge queue quietened and the matrix presumably completed inside 70 minutes). open.summary: Clozapine canary answers were discarded because table extraction interleaved the columns; extractor fixed, corpus re-index outstanding
open.detail: RESOLVED AS TO CAUSE 2026-09-16, by a live guest search of the production public corpus (read-only, user-authorised). CAUSE: page text came from page.get_text('text', sort=True), which orders text LINES by (y, x). A table whose cells wrap over several lines is therefore read straight ACROSS the columns. The served chunk from Clozapine Therapy - Initiation, Continuation and Ceasing Policy and Procedure (RKPG).pdf p16 reads 'Neutropenia Requires medical review. Stop clozapine. Contact WBC < 1.5 x 10 9/L. Flu-like symptoms such 3.2% haematologist ...', binding the withhold threshold to the word 'Contact' rather than to 'Neutropenia'. Answer verification correctly refused to state a clozapine threshold from that text. Nothing was wrong with retrieval, ranking, chunk splitting or any guard. EVIDENCE: the live search returned 12 chunks across 7 WA clozapine guidelines (FSH, CAMHS, RKPG, NMHS x2, AKG, FSH GP Shared Care), so the documents are retrievable and admitted; exactly one of the 12 bound a blood-count threshold to a stop instruction, and that one was the scrambled chunk. CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN EARLIER REPORTING: an interim analysis in the same session stated 'zero of twelve chunks bind a figure to an action'. That was WRONG. The detector used only ANC and neutrophil, while these WA guidelines say WBC, neutropenia and agranulocytosis. The correct count is one of twelve. The wrong count briefly supported a corpus-gap reading; it is recorded here so the number is not re-quoted. FOURTH DISPROVED THEORY, added to the two already in this row: 'the expected document is scoped uploaded_local and is unretrievable by design' is FALSE - retrieval returned these documents to an unauthenticated caller. The alias tables also already absorb the corpus renames, so a stale expectedFiles entry is not the cause either. FIXED IN CODE: extract_pdf_assets.table_aware_page_text substitutes the cell-by-cell rendering find_tables() already computes for detected grid regions, leaving surrounding prose in reading order, with a retention guard that keeps the raw text if detection would swallow the page and an ignore rule for heuristic non-grid candidates. Reproduced on a synthetic three-column table with wrapped cells, mutation-tested (removing the fix reproduces the exact production string), covered by worker/python/test_extract_pdf_assets_table_reading_order.py (5 tests) with the full worker suite green at 27 passed. STILL OUTSTANDING AND OPERATOR-ONLY: the fix only applies to documents ingested after it ships, so every already-indexed chunk keeps the scrambled wording until re-ingested. Step 6 of scripts/operator-clozapine-retrieval-diagnosis.sql lists the affected chunks and collapses them into a per-document re-index worklist, using two fingerprints validated against the real production text. The eval cases stay red until that re-index runs. DO NOT relax the cases, the verification predicate or adjacentLabelledNumericBandConflicts - the refusal is correct behaviour on corrupted evidence.

open.summary: WATCH: suspected CrCl/QTc NumberField corruption (not reproduced on 2026-09-13 retest)
open.detail: Earlier live desktop pass on psychiatry.tools prescribing mode: CrCl typed as 95 briefly displayed 42095; QTc showed unexpected 420. Suspected race in clinical-dashboard patient-profile NumberField (type=number + render sync) with writePatientProfile on every keystroke. 2026-09-13 re-verification could NOT reproduce (CrCl 95 and QTc 450 displayed correctly under slow type, replace, backspace). SaMD memo discusses broader patient-profile classification but does not evidence this corruption. Keep OPEN as a low-priority watch until Playwright digit-by-digit asserts values never gain foreign prefixes — do NOT treat as confirmed P1 clinical defect without reproduction. Stop: do not close from a single non-repro session alone; do not divert urgent clinical-safety work on suspicion alone. REPRODUCED AND FIXED 2026-09-18. No longer a watch item - the mechanism was found, reproduced in jsdom with digit-by-digit typing, and fixed. The field compared the incoming value against the previous prop and skipped the re-sync entirely while the current text was out of range, so a refused entry stayed on screen forever. Decisive failing assertions before the fix: expected '420' to be '95' (one mounted panel showing a CrCl the profile does not hold, while dosing alerts run on the other value) and expected '1' to be '1.0'. THE SECOND ONE IS WORSE AND WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY KNOWN: the sync re-derived the text from the stored number, so an in-progress '1.0' serum creatinine was rewritten to '1' under the caret and the next keystroke landed as 12 - and 12 mg/dL is in range, so it stored with no warning at all. An order-of-magnitude dosing input error, entered silently by a clinician who typed 1.02. THE FIX compares the incoming value against what the field last committed rather than against the previous prop, which separates the field's own write echoing through the shared store from news arriving elsewhere; an echo leaves the draft alone, news is adopted even over an out-of-range draft. Bounds, persistence and the error text are unchanged, and out-of-range text is still held for correction in place. Six new DOM cases cover CrCl, QTc, the multi-mount desync, the decimal path and a leading zero; three of them fail without the fix. REMAINDER RAISED SEPARATELY: a refused entry still survives a clear performed from another mounted panel (drafted fix held back because it changes when inputs remount), and the single-mount case of typing into a box that visibly still has text, which is a design decision rather than a defect. The standing clinical question - what a number field should do with a partial entry - is the PATIENT-NUMERIC-FIELD-DISPLAY open assurance decision in docs/clinical-hazard-controls.json.

open.summary: The Rockingham Peel clozapine guideline appears to state WBC below 1.5 for neutropenia, which is an ANC figure, and the evidence points at the source PDF rather than our extraction
open.detail: CLINICAL GOVERNANCE, NOT A SOFTWARE DEFECT, and it is the reason the extraction fix alone does not close this out. ANALYSIS 2026-09-16 from live public-corpus evidence. The served chunk of Clozapine Therapy - Initiation, Continuation and Ceasing Policy and Procedure (RKPG).pdf p16 states 'Neutropenia ... WBC < 1.5 x 10 9/L' and 'Agranulocytosis ... WBC < 0.5 x 10 9/L'. Those are ANC figures. Australian practice: ANC below 1.5 x10^9/L is the red result requiring cessation, ANC below 0.5 defines agranulocytosis, and the WBC red threshold is 3.0 with green at WBC at or above 3.5 and ANC at or above 2.0. WHY THIS IS PROBABLY THE DOCUMENT AND NOT OUR PIPELINE, which is the whole point of this row: the line-major interleaving fixed in extract_pdf_assets splices whole LINES between columns, so it can move a line to the wrong place but it can never rewrite a word or split within a line. In the live text the run 'WBC < 1.5 x 10 9/L. Flu-like symptoms such' appears uninterrupted, bounded by 'Contact' before it and '3.2%' after it, both of which are fragments from other columns. That makes it a single source line from a single cell, so the label WBC and the value 1.5 were adjacent in the PDF itself. CORROBORATION from three other WA guidelines in the same corpus, extracted by the same pipeline: Clozapine Prescribing (NMHS) gives neutrophils at or above 2.0 and WBC at or above 3.5; Clozapine Prescribing, Administration and Monitoring (AKG) gives WBC at or above 3.5; Clozapine Therapy - Initiation and Continuation (FSH) gives neutrophils above 2.0, WBC above 3.5 and WBC below 3.0. Every one of them pairs WBC with 3.0 or 3.5 and neutrophils with 2.0. NONE pairs WBC with 1.5. RKPG is the outlier. CONFIDENCE: high, not certain. This is reasoning from extracted text of a document nobody on this side has opened. A clinician must read the source PDF before anything is escalated. NEXT STEPS: (1) read RKPG p16 in the original; (2) if it does say WBC below 1.5, raise it with Rockingham Peel Group as a clinical document error, because clinicians are reading that PDF directly and independently of this system; (3) only then decide what this knowledge base should do about the document, options being flag it, supersede it, or restrict it. DO NOT hand-edit corpus text to correct a source document. DO NOT relax the clozapine eval cases. The system refusing to answer clozapine threshold questions from this passage is the correct and protective behaviour, and it stays correct even after the re-index if the underlying document is genuinely wrong.

open.summary: Drift def_hash normaliser strips from any '--' to end of line, hiding 91 percent of the P03 seed function
open.detail: schema_drift_snapshot() computes a function def_hash as md5 of pg_get_functiondef with block comments, then '--[^\n]*', then all whitespace removed (supabase/migrations/20260706200000_schema_drift_snapshot.sql:89 and the 20260818090000 history-probe rewrite:97). The line-comment regex cannot tell a real comment from '--' inside a string literal. public.site_content_registry_baseline embeds the whole registry seed as a single-line dollar-quoted JSON blob, and the first '--' falls at offset 176107 inside a service URL (Next-Step---Drug-and-Alcohol-Services), so 91.1 percent of the definition - 1841007 normalised chars down to 164524 - is stripped before hashing. Measured, not inferred: replaying both the old and the new function body into a local Postgres 16 produced the identical pinned hash c2dc2183657bab3c994af7f18ddfcb9b even though the bodies differ, and that same replay reproduces the manifest value exactly for the unchanged body, so the control is sound. Consequence: check:drift and the post-merge live-drift workflow cannot see a change to that function's seed data after the first '--'. Every other function loses only genuine comments, which is the intended behaviour. A fix has to distinguish a comment from a literal - dollar-quoted bodies could be hashed unstripped, or the strip applied only outside string literals - and it changes def_hash for every function, so it needs a manifest regeneration in the same change.

open.summary: The Caring Contacts production session cookie has no replay protection, and no sign-on service exists to issue one
open.detail: FOUND 2026-09-17 while verifying the external audit against the code (its finding C2), and half-addressed in PR #2860. The signature is verified with timingSafeEqual and exp IS enforced against an injectable clock, but there is no jti, no nonce, no issued-at, no session version and no revocation list, and no server-side store to check one against. So a captured cookie is replayable by anyone holding it until it expires, and a compromised session cannot be revoked before then. ALSO NOTE: the production session's role vocabulary is filtered through isDemoRole (session.ts:233), so live roles are the demo role list. That is probably fine and probably deliberate, but it is undocumented and worth a decision. NEXT: decide the cookie's claim set WITH the sign-on integration, not before it - the issuer's capabilities decide what is available (a jti needs somewhere to record it; a short TTL plus refresh may be cheaper than revocation). STOP: do not add a claim to signProductionSession speculatively. Nothing consumes it today and a half-designed token is harder to replace than none.

open.summary: site_content_release_records_immutable is not 'enable always', so session_replication_role = replica bypasses the freeze's only structural protection
open.detail: READ FROM THE SCHEMA ON 2026-09-16, NOT EXPLOITED OR TESTED. supabase/schema.sql:12722-12724 creates site_content_release_records_immutable as an ordinary row trigger (before update or delete ... execute function guard_site_content_immutable_row). PostgreSQL does not fire an ordinary trigger when session_replication_role = 'replica', so a session that sets that GUC can UPDATE or DELETE rows of the frozen epoch-zero release with nothing raising. That is not a theoretical technique in this repository: scripts/check-site-content-control-plane.mjs:889-894 uses exactly it against a sibling table. TWO FURTHER GAPS IN THE SAME SEAL: the trigger covers only UPDATE and DELETE, so nothing prevents a row being INSERTED into a retained bootstrap release (it need only satisfy site_content_release_records_check1), and TRUNCATE is a statement-level event a row trigger never sees. Until the catalogue read-latency migration lands, the per-read bootstrap digest recomputation is the only thing that detects an inserted row, and it detects it after the fact — see docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS, stated honestly: setting session_replication_role needs the same superuser or postgres privilege an attacker would need to write the rows anyway, and such an attacker could equally replace the digest function. So the value here is against ACCIDENT — a half-applied migration, a bad replay, a partial restore, or a script that sets the GUC for an unrelated reason and then touches this table — not against a determined adversary. THE FIX: 'alter table public.site_content_release_records enable always trigger site_content_release_records_immutable', plus an 'enable always' before-insert trigger restricted to the retained bootstrap release ids and an 'enable always' before-truncate statement trigger. All transactional, no index build. SEQUENCE IT WITH the read-latency migration, which needs the same seal to justify removing the per-read digest; doing it separately means doing the same CREATE TRIGGER lock twice. GATE: SQL, so it ships as a new forward migration and needs an approved merge window. RUN check:site-content-control-plane in Docker FIRST — its own fixtures rely on session_replication_role on a sibling table, and an 'enable always' trigger on this one must be proven not to break them before merging.

open.summary: site_content_canonical_json is recursive plpgsql, so release activation will slow the same way the read path did once a release exceeds a couple of thousand records
open.detail: READ FROM THE SQL ON 2026-09-16, NOT MEASURED. site_content_canonical_json (supabase/schema.sql:12746) is a recursive plpgsql function: one invocation per JSON node, and a string_agg subquery over jsonb_each or jsonb_array_elements at every container. It defines EVERY fingerprint in the site-content control plane — release digest, contentHash, publicationVersion, governance and lineage hashes, plan and receipt identities — and is reimplemented in JS and pinned by tests/site-content-p03-baseline.test.ts, so it cannot be rewritten without invalidating stored digests across the live database. Measured proxy for its cost: the 843-record epoch-zero freeze canonicalises to 9,522,923 bytes across 164,820 JSON nodes (55,103 containers), i.e. ~165k plpgsql invocations and ~55k planned aggregate subqueries per pass, and two such passes per HTTP request cost about four seconds against live — see docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md. The read path is being fixed by removing the calls. The WRITE path cannot be: site_content_dynamic_state_digest, site_content_release_digest, stage_site_content_sync_event, activate_site_content_release and rollback_site_content_release all canonicalise the full release by design and must keep doing so. Today that is tolerable because activation is rare and operator-driven. It scales linearly in node count, so a release of 2,000+ records makes activation slow in exactly the same way, and an activation that exceeds its statement timeout fails a publication rather than a page view. WHAT TO DO: nothing yet — this is a recorded scaling limit, not a defect. BEFORE the catalogue grows materially past the freeze, time one activation against a realistic release on a local Postgres (npm run check:site-content-control-plane already replays the control plane in Docker) and record the node-count-to-seconds curve, so the ceiling is known before an operator hits it mid-publication. DO NOT rewrite site_content_canonical_json to a set-based or C-backed equivalent as a performance fix: any byte-level difference changes every stored fingerprint, and a C extension cannot be installed by migration on Supabase.

open.summary: read_site_content_health() canonicalises the whole frozen corpus several times in one call
open.detail: COUNTED FROM THE SQL TEXT ON 2026-09-16, NOT MEASURED. Inside read_site_content_health() (supabase/schema.sql:15112-15342) there are four site_content_bootstrap_digest call sites — :15184 and :15185 in the bootstrap CTE (release_digest and dynamic_state_digest, which are equal for the bootstrap release) and :15285 and :15286 in the rollback CTE — plus two further whole-release aggregates via site_content_release_digest and a direct site_content_dynamic_state_digest. Each whole-corpus evaluation canonicalises 9,522,923 bytes and 164,820 JSON nodes through site_content_canonical_json, a recursive plpgsql function with one invocation per node, so each pass is roughly 165k plpgsql invocations and 55k planned aggregate subqueries. One investigation put the repeat count at five; four bootstrap_digest sites is what the current mirror contains, and how many are actually EVALUATED per call depends on planner materialisation and on which branches are reachable — nobody has measured it. THE FIX, and it is small: fold each PAIR that compares two stored columns to the same freshly computed digest into one evaluation (a scalar subquery or lateral computing the digest once and comparing both columns to it). No semantic change, roughly halves the work. RELATED: ledger #458SAC records the measured ~7s cost of this RPC against live and its 24 failed production deploys between 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-14, and asks for an EXPLAIN baseline; this row is the concrete mechanism and fix that #458SAC's next action was looking for, and the two should be read together. WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: the RPC is deliberately off the readiness path (src/lib/health-response.ts:148-158), so this is cost on the token-gated deep health probe and check:production-readiness, not on any user request. GATE: this is a SQL change, so it ships as a new forward migration and needs an approved merge window; run check:migration-role and check:function-grants, and regenerate the drift manifest. Context: docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md.

open.summary: A refused patient number still survives a profile clear performed from another mounted panel
open.detail: REMAINDER OF #WFARS3, deliberately not fixed in the 2026-09-18 PR that fixed the main defect. The NumberField sync now adopts a real value arriving from elsewhere, so a panel can no longer display a CrCl the profile does not hold. TWO ROUTES REMAIN OPEN. (1) A CLEAR IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REJECTION. A refused out-of-range entry stores null, and so does a profile-wide clear, so the field cannot tell 'my entry was refused' from 'the whole profile was wiped by another mounted copy of the panel, or by sign-out'. Reproduced: panel A holds a refused CrCl 420, panel B clears the profile, and A still shows 420. Typing 95 into it then reads 42095 - the originally reported symptom. THE FIX IS KNOWN AND DRAFTED: a clearGeneration counter incremented in clearPatientProfile and a new resetPatientProfile in src/lib/patient-profile-storage.ts, surfaced through patient-profile-context.tsx via useSyncExternalStore, and used as the resetNonce in patient-profile-panel.tsx so every mount remounts its entry fields on any clear. It was held back because it changes when inputs remount - they would now also remount on a sign-out clear, which destroys and rebuilds the input elements and so drops focus if a field happened to be focused at that instant. Clears are deliberate and infrequent, so the exposure looks nil, but it is a behaviour change outside the typing path and wants a deliberate decision. (2) THE SINGLE-MOUNT CASE IS NOT A CODE DEFECT. If a clinician gets a refused 420 into the box and, without clearing it, clicks at the end and types 95, they see 42095 - that is simply typing into a box that already had text, and the field is red throughout. Closing it needs a design decision (clear refused text on blur, or a visible clear-this-field control), not a bug fix. NEXT: decide (2) as a product question, then land (1) with the drafted patch plus the seventh DOM test that was written for it and held back with it.
